results.summary: WilfTT is an 8-bit counter design that increments on each clock cycle. It is implemented in Wokwi and runs at 1 Hz. The design is tested by pressing play in the simulation. The project lacks detailed documentation, so its specific operation and any external hardware requirements are unclear.

This project implements a 3-bit ALU that can perform AND, OR, XOR, and ADD operations based on a 2-bit opcode. It takes two 3-bit operands and outputs a 3-bit result along with carry and zero flags. The design computes all operations in parallel and selects the output using a multiplexer. Testing involves setting the inputs and opcode and verifying the outputs; external hardware such as DIP switches and LEDs can be used.

This design, titled Tiny Tapeout Novomorphic Design 1, implements two logic gates: XOR and AND. It takes two inputs and produces both XOR and AND outputs simultaneously. The truth table is provided for testing, and no external hardware is required. It serves as a simple educational example of basic gates.

TT-wokwi-template is a design based on the Wokwi template that increments a counter from 0 to 9 on a screen when a STEP button is pressed. The pin names and documentation are vague, with no clear description of the hardware or functionality. The external hardware is listed as unknown. The project appears to be a template with minimal custom logic.

This project, Tom Haley Tiny Tape Out Design, has no documentation whatsoever; all fields, including pin names and descriptions, are marked as TBD. There is no indication of what the design does or how it should be tested. No external hardware is specified. It is effectively a placeholder.

Arran's tinytapeout project implements a single 2-input NAND gate. The design takes two input pins and produces the NAND output on one output pin. Testing is done by changing the inputs and observing the output according to NAND logic. No external hardware is required; it is a basic educational demonstration.

This design takes two 4-bit inputs, adds them, and converts the 5-bit result (including carry) to a hexadecimal representation for a 7-segment display. It outputs the seven segment control signals plus a decimal point. The design is tested by applying two 4-bit numbers and checking the displayed sum. External hardware includes switch banks for input and a 7-segment display for output.

This workshop design includes AND, NAND, and OR gates, plus a clock divider that uses 16 flip-flops to produce divided clock outputs at the 12th and 16th stages. It takes three inputs (a, b, c) and provides several outputs. The logic gates are tested with a truth table, and the clock divider can be observed with a 10 kHz clock. External hardware such as LEDs can be used to visualize the outputs.

This project enables testing of various logic gates by turning switches on and off to achieve specific outcomes. Some inputs and outputs are interconnected between gates, allowing exploration of logic behavior. The design has 8 inputs and 8 outputs, all labeled as logic input/output. External hardware includes switches and a single-digit LED display for observing results.

This test file for WOKWI implements OR and AND gates, with a 7-segment display driven by a 10 kHz clock. It takes two inputs and outputs the OR and AND results. The documentation is minimal and does not explain how the 7-segment display is used. It appears to be a template or test design for the Wokwi environment.
